listing.title: Hand Carved and Painted TAGUA NUT BABY IN A NUT from Hong Kong Rare Vintage
listing.description: Hand Carved and Painted TAGUA NUT BABY IN A NUT from Hong Kong Rare Vintage Grown in Zambia/Zaire, Sent to China where they're carved, Sold in Hong Kong at Jade Market which is a huge seller of all kinds of items you can't get anywhere else. THIS ONE IS LIKE A BABY WRAPPED UP IN A TAGUA NUT. So, in this case, you can see what a tagua nut looks like, because the baby is carved into the side of it, and the rest of it remains. I assume it's polished up pretty well. (It does not come with the wooden display stand.) The Tagua nuts were harvested in Zambia (Africa) and then sent to China for carving. The Tagua tree is a palm tree that grows freely in some subtropical climates, but is absolutely not grown in China. The Tagua nut is very hard and takes on a beautiful ivory or darker than ivory, amber color. For this reason, Tagua is sometimes known as Vegetable Ivory. The composition of the Tagua nut is so similar to mammal tusk that it is difficult for some people to tell them apart. For me, I feel like I can easily tell them apart. The carved tagua nuts I'm selling here are wonderful, but I don't think they look like they are creme-color, or light enough to be mistaken for ivory. Perhaps they have turned to amber over time? I think these carved pieces, bigger than buckeyes, are over 25 years old. The lady from whom I acquired them traveled to Hong Kong, China, Japan and various other Asian places and elsewhere in the world on shopping excursions quite often. She must've been NUTS a

evidence.summary: CITES listing for African or Asian elephant ivory: Asian elephant: Appendix I.

data.cites: Asian elephant: Appendix I. African elephant: Appendix I, except the populations of Botswana, Namibia, South Africa and Zimbabwe, which are in Appendix II with an annotation that restricts trade in their ivory.

evidence.summary: Interstate sale of African elephant ivory is prohibited except ESA antiques (at least 100 years old, not repaired with ivory since Dec 27, 1973, imported through an antique port where applicable) and de minimis items (ivory under 200 grams, not more than 50% of the item by volume or value, made before July 6, 2016, with import-date conditions) (applies because the item ships from US-IL).

data.rule: Interstate sale of African elephant ivory is prohibited except ESA antiques (at least 100 years old, not repaired with ivory since Dec 27, 1973, imported through an antique port where applicable) and de minimis items (ivory under 200 grams, not more than 50% of the item by volume or value, made before July 6, 2016, with import-date conditions). Intrastate sale is allowed federally only with proof of lawful import before Jan 18, 1990; states may be stricter.
